answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that vests over a long horizon, so a fake identity costs real capital and time. Reputation then grows like a vine: trust spreads only through verified work with established peers, never by self-declaration. A newcomer starts in a small garden of low-value tasks and earns access to larger jobs only after consistent, attested performance, making mass fake identities expensive and slow while honest agents compound credibility.
